title: Mastering Eyelid Laceration & Wound Repair
summary: A comprehensive guide to the surgical restoration of adnexal integrity. This poster covers everything from basic marginal alignment to complex canalicular reconstruction and tissue loss management, essential for any ophthalmic surgeon.

sections.title: Clinical Overview & Goals
sections.content: Eyelid wound repair focuses on restoring three-dimensional anatomy while preserving globe protection and aesthetic symmetry. The primary goals are anatomical alignment (especially the lid margin), maintaining a smooth posterior surface to prevent corneal abrasion, and ensuring dynamic function (levator and orbicularis integrity).

sections.title: Immediate Red Flags
content: Signs of Open Globe (Peaked pupil, Seidel positive)
Orbital Compartment Syndrome (Proptosis + High IOP)
Fat Prolapse (Indicates Orbital Septum breach)
Marcus-Gunn Pupil (Optic Nerve involvement)
Foreign Body Sensation (Suspect Intraocular FB)

sections.title: Pre-Operative Workup
content: Step 1: Visual Acuity assessment (Medico-legal priority).
Step 2: Rule out ruptured globe and intraocular foreign bodies via Slit Lamp.
Step 3: Evaluate Lid Margin and Canalicular involvement using Bowman probes if needed.
Step 4: Assess Levator function (Excursion) to rule out aponeurosis dehiscence.
Step 5: CT Orbit (thin cuts) if high-velocity injury or metal-on-metal suspected.

sections.title: Repair of Marginal Lacerations
content: 1. Placement of the 'Master Suture' at the Grey Line (6-0 Silk) to align margin.
2. Placement of Lash Line and Posterior Margin sutures (long ends left for traction).
3. Interrupted Tarsal sutures (5-0 Vicryl) - MUST NOT pass through conjunctiva.
4. Skin closure (6-0 Nylon or Gut).
5. Tie marginal suture ends over the skin sutures to prevent corneal irritation.

content.explanation: S: Symmetry of lash line; T: Tarsal alignment; I: Inversion avoidance (Everting sutures); T: Tension-free closure; C: Canalicular check; H: Hemostasis.

sections.title: Dog Bites: Special Protocols
content: Copious irrigation (Normal Saline/Betadine)
Prophylactic Augmentin (Amoxicillin-Clavulanate)
Check Tetanus Status
Rabies post-exposure prophylaxis if animal unknown
Primary closure is generally preferred in the face due to vascularity

sections.title: Post-Operative Care
content: Antibiotic Ointment (Erythromycin/Bacitracin) TID
Cool compresses for first 48 hours to minimize edema
Suture removal: Skin (5-7 days), Marginal (10-14 days)
Avoid heavy lifting or straining (Valsalva)
Protect eye with a shield if globe integrity was a concern

sections.title: Clinical Pearls (High Yield)
content: Always 'evert' the wound edges to account for future scar contraction (prevent notching).
The 'Grey Line' is your most important anatomical landmark for marginal repair.
If the canalicular system is involved, repair it BEFORE the eyelid skin.
Never use cautery near the lid margin; it can lead to permanent lash loss and lid notching.

sections.title: Landmark Studies: Bionic Lids?
sections.content: Recent advances emphasize the use of 2-Octyl Cyanoacrylate (Dermabond) for non-tension skin wounds. Studies show equivalent aesthetic outcomes to sutures with reduced procedure time. In canalicular trauma, the 'Masterka' stent (suture-less) is gaining traction for ease of insertion and reduced nasal trauma.
